content:
alex (Finance): FYI Tierflip pilot quote just landed. Need clarity on tiering, overage calc, and whether pilot credits roll into renewal. Looping in procurement + eng for PO implications.

vendor-rep (Tierflip): Thanks Alex — hi all. Quick summary: 3mo pilot, 50k tokens/month included, UI seats unlimited. Overage $0.0008/token. Pilot credits are promotional and do not automatically convert to committed credits. We can add concessions for renewal.

maria (Procurement): Clarifying: any implicit minimum commit or convert-to-commit clause on renewal? We need options that fit enterprise procurement.

vendor-rep (Tierflip): No minimum during pilot. For renewal: standard plans offer up to 50% discount with a 6mo commit. We can offer a 3mo bridge that allows rollover of up to 20% unused pilot credits if you sign within 30 days of pilot end.

kevin (EngOps): How are overages measured across different workloads — streaming chat vs batch embeddings? Our usage mix matters.

vendor-rep (Tierflip): Streaming/chat is token-based; embeddings are counted per vector. We can provide per-endpoint metering so embeddings and chat show separate line items. Example in quote: embeddings = vectors * 1 unit, chat = tokens * 1 unit.

sanjay (Platform): We require invoice-level detail: per-endpoint and per-model breakdown, plus CSV export for our internal recon. Is that supported?

vendor-rep (Tierflip): Yes — invoices can include per-model & per-route lines, and we support CSV export via SFTP.

alex (Finance): Procurement: we need a hard cap on monthly overages for the pilot. Any overage > $12k/mo will require explicit PO approval. @maria please advise.

procurement-bot: Reminder: vendor agreements over $25k require Legal review and a signed SOW. See /procure-guidelines for thresholds.

maria (Procurement): We can request a hard cap of $12k/mo and alerting at 75% usage. Would Tierflip be willing to add throttling/alerting and a discount to overage under that cap?

vendor-rep (Tierflip): Standard alerts at 70/85/95% are available. Throttling (rate-limit fallback) is optional. We can accept a $12k cap if we add a 10% discount on overage charges under that cap and agree to send usage alerts.

kevin (EngOps): Important: throttling should return graceful 429 + Retry-After. We prefer fallback to a lower-cost model rather than hard failures.

vendor-rep (Tierflip): Agreed — 429 with Retry-After is our default. We can also configure an automatic fallback route to a cheaper model for degraded performance instead of failing.

alex (Finance): Cool. Next steps: maria will engage Legal for SOW/PO path, Sanjay to provide endpoint list + expected monthly tokens, Kevin to confirm fallback model acceptable. Vendor to provide machine-readable quote.

maria (Procurement): I'll open a legal ticket and request redlines. Can the updated quote be provided as CSV/JSON for our procurement system?

vendor-rep (Tierflip): Yes — sending updated quote as CSV + JSON by EOD with line items and renewal options.

sanjay (Platform): I'll compile expected usage: rough estimate — chat 800k tokens/mo, embeddings 120k vectors/mo, rerank <5k. Will post a spreadsheet.

alex (Finance): :thumbsup: Keep the per-model invoice requirement firm — if we can't get that, procurement won't sign.

vendor-rep (Tierflip): Understood. We'll include per-model lines and the alerting + cap language in the next draft.

alex (Finance): Thanks everyone — please update thread when quote lands.
